summary: An agent asks the user for a secret through the Switchboard MCP tool request_secret. The chat shows a card with a masked input; Switchboard writes the value to a private 0600 file for that chat only and tells the agent the file path and the env var SWITCHBOARD_SECRETS_DIR, never the value. Step 1: the file store (main/secrets/secret-store.ts) and the agent_secret_dirs and agent_secrets tables. Step 2: the request_secret tool on the MCP server while the flag is on (refused in plan mode, from an open child chat, past 3 open cards or 5 requests in 10 minutes, and for any unknown or out-of-range field), sbsec_ cards in the approval card broker (request.opened.secretRequest, a plain detail with no title for older clients and push), saves only through ProviderRegistry.answerAgentSecret (a failed save keeps the card open; an approval on the generic respond channel is refused), result turns with the path and env var, SWITCHBOARD_SECRETS_DIR in every agent kind's env at session start, a Stop that keeps the card and the files, an archive that closes the card and deletes the files, and extend and delete now. Step 3: the desktop card (renderer SecretRequestCard: header, title, plain-text instructions with the URL host in bold and an open confirm, an uncontrolled password input with a 10-second show button, Save securely and Decline, the footer with the ttl and the SSH machine, the provider-key note), its answer channel agent-secret:answer, extend, delete and list (admin scope, strict argument shapes, flag-gated, Extend and Delete now only on the asking chat's own secrets, list without values), the channels kept out of perf spans and the reconnect queue, and the one-line Saved, Declined and expired states with Extend and Delete now. Step 4: redaction. While a file lives the backend holds its value in memory for that chat (secrets/secret-redactor.ts: armed on save and read back from the live file by the store's sweep at start, zero-filled on delete, expiry, archive and sweep; values under 8 characters are not matched) and masks the exact value, its base64 and base64url forms and its URL-encoded form as [secret NAME]: in every runtime event before the registry stores or publishes it (secrets/runtime-event-redaction.ts, with a carry of the longest pattern less one character for streamed deltas, flushed with the thread's next event), in changed-file cards (which then offer no Accept or Reject), in every row written to the messages table and so the FTS index (db/messages.ts), and in every history read (conversations/history.ts: phone and desktop windows, the full read behind export, fork anchors, the handoff preamble and the tool-call lookup). A hit adds one system row per turn, naming the file for a changed-file hit. Step 5: the phones show the card read-only whenever request.opened carries secretRequest (only a backend that advertises agent_secret_request_v1 sends it): the header that the agent asked, the title, the instructions as plain text with each URL host in bold, Answer this on your computer, and Decline, which goes through the existing provider:respond-to-request as a deny with no value (a phone's approve is refused). The result row shows as one line, Saved, Declined or expired, with no Extend or Delete now; older clients show the plain detail. Step 6 (this change): usage counts and docs. Six closed-list events, sent only while the flag is on and analytics is on: secret_request.opened (agent kind, ttl, remote) and refused (plan, child, cap, invalid) from the tool, answered (saved or declined, a time bucket) and closed (expired, withdrawn, archived, deleted) from the card's result and the file's end, extended (the how-many-th Extend: 1, 2, 3 or more) and masked (tool, text or diff, with the masked row, so once per turn). No event carries a name, title, instructions, value, length or hash. docs/features.md describes the feature, what it cannot promise and how to turn it on. The desktop slice and the backend contract are complete; the flag stays off by default, and the phones stay read-only until phone entry (agent_secret_phone_v1).

reactNativeIos.followUpRelease: Phone entry of a value, capability agent_secret_phone_v1 (design section 7.3): a pinned wss:// connection, a Face ID or passcode gate before the input shows, the value sealed to a one-time X25519 key from the card, and secure text entry with no autofill or keyboard learning. Until then the phone shows the card read-only, and only while agent_secret_request is on.

hardware: The migration ran against a copy of a real 1.1 GB profile database (1,450 conversations): both tables were created and PRAGMA integrity_check answered ok.
notExercised: tmutil addexclusion was not checked against a real Time Machine setup; tests inject the exclusion step.

Codex sandbox modes (read-only, workspace-write) read any file by default and Claude's sandbox mode prompts per tool with no OS sandbox, so no read allow list was added; this was read from the adapters, not run.

No packaged build has run the card yet (high-risk rule): the save, extend and delete paths were checked by unit and jsdom tests only, not on a packaged app with existing user data or through a real SSH tunnel.
The card's look in the dark, light and translucent themes was not compared against the mock in a screenshot test.

Redaction does not change what the model saw or the provider's own JSONL transcript: a command that prints the value puts it in the model's context and in that file. Our copies are masked only while the secret file lives; after it is deleted or expires, history rows read from the provider transcript show the value again (stored rows stay masked).
A value inside a larger base64 blob at an offset that is not a multiple of 3 bytes, or encoded in any other way (hex, JSON escapes of quotes or backslashes, shell quoting), is not matched.
The canary ran in unit tests only, not by hand on a packaged build against logs/, the database WAL file and a phone over a real connection.
The phone card was not exercised on iOS hardware or in the simulator; only jest renders it.
The phone card was not exercised on Android hardware; only Robolectric renders it.
A phone cannot read the saved list, so its Saved line never turns into expired or deleted when the file goes.
The phone push text ("An agent asks for a secret" and the chat name) was not checked on iOS or Android hardware; only unit tests build it.

The analytics collector does not list the secret_request events yet, so it rejects them until it is updated; no event has reached it. The headless server on an SSH machine configures no analytics, so a remote backend sends no counts and remote is never sent as true today.
The extend count is kept in memory per backend run, so a restart starts it again at 1.
